problemStatement.formal: Define f(n) = ∑_{p<n} 1/(n-p). Is lim inf f(n) = 1? Is lim sup f(n) = ∞? Is f(n) = o(log log n)?
problemStatement.plain: How does the sum of reciprocal distances from n to primes below n behave?
whyMatters: Connects prime distribution near n to analytic behavior of a natural sum
Average behavior known (de Bruijn-Erdős-Turán) but extremal behavior open
Links to prime gaps and density of primes in short intervals

proven: de Bruijn-Erdős-Turán: ∑_{n<x} f(n) ~ x (f averages to 1)
f(n) ≥ 0 for all n (proved in Lean)
Dense primes in [n, n+n^c] with c > 0 implies lim inf f(n) > 0
open: Q3: Is f(n) = o(log log n)?
∑_{p<x} f(p)² ~ π(x) (sum restricted to prime arguments)
